subject: Materials Science
title: HCP: Hexagonal Close-Packed
description: A micro-lesson that makes HCP: Hexagonal Close-Packed usable.

hook.text: Titanium is light and strong but hard to form — blame its hexagonal crystal structure.

buildup.text: HCP stacks hexagonal layers in an ABAB pattern — atoms nestle into valleys of the layer below.

discovery.text: Like FCC, HCP is 74% packed — maximum density — but with far fewer slip systems.

twist.text: Only three easy slip systems makes HCP metals brittle at room temperature compared to FCC.

climax.text: Titanium, zinc, and magnesium are all HCP — each strong but tricky to shape.

punchline.text: Same packing density as FCC, but hexagons don't slide as easily.

quiz.question: Why are HCP metals less ductile than FCC metals?
options: HCP metals are less densely packed
HCP has fewer available slip systems
